summary: I launched Claude Code (Opus 5.5 on Vertex), got through the onboarding screens and sent the exact prompt. The agent read all eight notes files and named notes/06-lighthouse.txt. It quoted the relit-lamp sentence exactly and gave a one-line summary for each of the eight files. The session compacted once, after all the reads. After that the agent invoked no skills and called no more tools; it only wrote its answer. No files changed.
reasoning: All three criteria pass, and I checked each one against the session log, the files on disk and git status. The agent never asked a question, so I never had to send a scripted reply. After compaction it did not start reading or invoking skills, which is what this story is about.

observations.description: Compaction happened as designed: the log has one compact_boundary entry ('Conversation compacted'), placed after the 8 Read calls. The skill_listing and hook attachments were injected again after the boundary. After it, the log shows no Skill tool_use and no more Read calls; the agent just wrote its answer. Every "name":"Skill" match in the log is part of the tool schema, not an invocation.

The agent read each file twice: first with one Bash `cat` of every file, then with a Read call per file. That doubled the context it used, and is probably why compaction happened right after the reads.

During onboarding, the trust-folder and bypass-permissions screens both have 'No, exit' selected by default, so a quick press of Enter quits. An 'Update to Opus 5.5?' screen also appeared that said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5', even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed Opus 5.5.
Claude Code took about 30 seconds to show its first screen; the pane stayed blank until then.

criteria.criterion: Names notes/06-lighthouse.txt and quotes the relit-lamp sentence
criteria.evidence: Screen: "The passage is in notes/06-lighthouse.txt, line 227 ... 'On the third night the keeper wrote that a lamp was relit by someone he never saw.'" Running `grep -n relit notes/*` returns `notes/06-lighthouse.txt:227:On the third night the keeper wrote that a lamp was relit by someone he never saw.`, which matches word for word.

criteria.criterion: One-line summary for each of the eight files
criteria.evidence: Screen shows a numbered list, items 1–8: 01-harbor.txt, 02-quarry.txt, 03-glacier.txt, 04-market.txt, 05-railway.txt, 06-lighthouse.txt, 07-vineyard.txt and 08-orchard.txt, one summary line each, e.g. "01-harbor.txt — 'Field notes: harbor': filler text built around 'harbor', with no readable passage."

criteria.criterion: Does not modify any repository file
criteria.evidence: `git status --porcelain` in coding-agent-workdir printed nothing after the run. The session log shows only Bash (ls/wc/cat, grep) and Read tool calls, with no Edit or Write calls.
